title: Minimax Design for Relative Efficacy with a Sparse Unknown Baseline Event Count
banked_reason: Sound delivered reduction package is below the field floor: kernel_substituted@oeq:sharp-efficacy-frontier; evaluated first nonzero correction remains open; paper_score_ceiling 4.5 < 7.4; no bounded fix in scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is a specialized unrestricted count reduction, finite-band minimax certificate, and exact k=1 endpoint saddle, which earns subfield rather than field. For growing k, the note proves only the upper bound 4/k+O(k^(-3/2)); neither the leading minimax constant nor any first nonzero correction has a matching converse. The reference-risk expansion, endpoint Bayes calculations, and posterior square identity leave the decisive posterior gain and global attaining estimator unresolved. The two-order transfer theorem assumes the matching expansions it transfers, while the distinct SATE results of [Hull](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.09812v1) and [Sudijono–Dobriban–Tchetgen Tchetgen](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13822v1) cannot supply them. The framing explicitly acknowledges these gaps and contains no stale assertion that the sharp frontier is established, but the advertised sharp efficacy precision benchmark remains undelivered. The projected score is constrained by that missing characterization, the absence of evaluated optimal planning procedures beyond k=1, and a rational enumeration certificate that establishes computability without demonstrating practical performance for larger bands. proof_attempt_summary: Three D0 rounds sharpened the exact original-record/count reduction, zero-error latent-allocation implementation, binary-color finite-cohort bound, fixed-band certificate, and k=1 saddle without changing assumptions or estimand. The math panel passed, but the promised evaluated sharp correction remains open in oeq:legal-posterior-profile and oeq:sharp-efficacy-frontier; the independent terminal gate confirmed incremental below the field floor. Banked downgraded under the standing operator rule; no Lean formalization, acceptance, or promotion was performed.
tldr: Relative efficacy divides a prevented-event count by an unknown baseline count. Under the stipulated public sparse band and individual no-harm, the unrestricted fixed-cohort design problem reduces to a logged-allocation two-count game in the fixed-band limit. The proved comparison is \(0\le r_k-R(n,k)\le\beta_{n,k}\le\varepsilon_{n,k}\). The collision probability \(\varepsilon_{n,k}=1-(n)_{2k}/n^{2k}\) is exact; \(\beta_{n,k}\) is a uniform bound obtained by also coupling binary treatment colors. For \(n\ge4k\), this gives a converse error of order \(k^{3/2}/n\). Every reduced procedure has an exact latent-allocation Bernoulli-mixture implementation with no risk increase, and a single legal prior controls all original designs. The evaluated first sharp correction remains unresolved through the legal posterior-profile and sharp efficacy-frontier questions.
gap: Unrestricted SATE minimax theory and relative-risk allocation theory do not establish the stipulated unknown-baseline efficacy correction.
fill: An evaluated two-order minimax expansion, a matching allocation and nonlinear rule, and a common legal original-table converse provide that benchmark.
